threads.thread_goal: Align on final tier structure, benefits, and pricing before documentation freeze.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the initial tier structure for A1 and would like to get feedback before we lock it in. We're looking at three tiers: Basic, Premium, and Elite. Each tier has different eligibility rules and benefit packages. The pricing bands are still being finalized with finance, but I wanted to share the framework first. Can everyone review and share thoughts on the tier naming and core benefits? T1 is underway and we need to close this by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks for getting this out. I've reviewed the draft and the three-tier approach makes sense from a sales perspective. The naming is clear and easy to communicate. One thing I'd flag: the Premium tier benefits seem a bit thin compared to what we discussed in the kickoff. Can we add early access to new features or priority support? That would help with positioning against competitors. Also, have we validated the pricing bands with finance yet? I want to make sure the incentive structure in T9 aligns with what we're proposing here.

I agree with the three-tier structure. The naming is straightforward. On the benefits, I think we should be careful not to over-promise. Let me check with the operations team on what we can actually deliver for Premium without stretching resources. I'll get back to you by tomorrow morning with a revised benefits list. The pricing bands—I'm still waiting on finance to confirm the margin impact analysis.

The tier structure looks reasonable. I do have a question on the eligibility rules for the Elite tier—are we basing it on annual spend, tenure, or both? This will affect how we target existing members in the launch campaign. Also, the Basic tier seems to have minimal benefits. Will that be attractive enough to convert new members, or is it mainly for retention of lower-value segments?

Good questions. The Elite tier eligibility is based on annual spend threshold plus tenure—we want to reward loyal, high-value members. For the Basic tier, you're right that it's lean, but the idea is to create a clear entry point and then upsell. We can refine this once we get feedback from the pilot in T10. Let me incorporate the feedback from 61232 on Premium benefits and 285875's operational constraints, and I'll have a revised version by tomorrow EOD.

That makes sense on the eligibility criteria. One more thing—once we finalize the benefits, we'll need to make sure the sales pitch in A2 reflects the value prop clearly. I'm already drafting the pitch framework in T2, so I'll align it with whatever we lock in here. Should we schedule a quick sync with the customer service team to make sure they understand the tier differences before we move to training? They'll be fielding a lot of questions on day one.

Good idea on syncing with customer service. I'll coordinate that once we have the final benefits locked. In the meantime, I'm working on the operations playbook in T3 to document how each tier flows through onboarding, upgrades, and cancellations. That will feed into A3 and should help everyone understand the mechanics.

Perfect. So here's what I'm hearing: we're aligned on three tiers with clear naming. We need to refine the Premium benefits to be more competitive, confirm Elite eligibility rules, and validate that Basic is sufficient as an entry point. 285875, can you get me the operational constraints by tomorrow morning? And 61232, once we have those, can you review the updated benefits against the pitch framework? I want to make sure everything is consistent before we move to D1 and D2.

Absolutely. I'll review the updated benefits against the pitch framework tomorrow and flag any gaps. Once we have the final list, I can also start drafting the objection-handling guide in T2 so we're ready for training. This is on track for the 21-day timeline.

I'll wait for the updated benefits list before finalizing the targeting strategy for the launch campaign. Once I see the final tiers and benefits, I can map out which segments fit best into each tier.

I'll have the operational constraints and revised benefits by 9 AM tomorrow. I'm also starting to think about the data fields we'll need in A4 to support these tiers—things like tier assignment date, upgrade/downgrade history, benefit usage tracking. I'll flag those in a separate thread once we finalize the tier structure.

Great thinking. Yes, let's tackle the data fields in TH3 once we have the tier structure locked. For now, let me summarize where we are: we're moving forward with three tiers (Basic, Premium, Elite), and we need final sign-off on the benefits and pricing by EOD tomorrow. 61232, can you confirm the pitch framework will be ready by end of week? And 285875, once you send the operational constraints, I'll update A1 and we can move to D1 and D2 approval.

Pitch framework will be ready by end of week. I'm also thinking about how to structure the training in T5 to make sure everyone understands not just the pitch, but the operational mechanics from A3. We should probably do a joint session with sales and membership teams so there's no confusion on the handoff.

Agreed. Joint training makes sense. We'll cover that in TH2 when we lock the training approach. For now, let's focus on getting the tier structure finalized. I'll send out the updated A1 by 10 AM tomorrow with the revised benefits and operational constraints incorporated. Everyone, please review and confirm by 2 PM so we can formally approve D1 and D2.

Understood. I'll have my input to you by 9 AM. One thing I want to flag: we should also think about how to handle tier downgrades if a member no longer qualifies. That's going to be a sensitive conversation, and we'll need clear guidance in A3 on how to approach it.
Good point. Downgrades are definitely a risk area. We should include that in the objection-handling guide in T2 and make sure the FAQ in T7 covers it. I'll add that to my list.

Excellent. So we have a clear path forward: finalize benefits and pricing by tomorrow 2 PM, then move to D1 and D2 approval. Once that's locked, we'll move to the sales pitch and training in TH2, and the data fields in TH3. Let me know if anyone has blockers.
No blockers from my end. I'm ready to move forward once the tier structure is finalized.

Perfect. I'm going to formally propose D1 and D2 for approval tomorrow at 3 PM once I've incorporated all feedback. D1 is the approval of the three-tier structure and naming convention in A1. D2 is the confirmation of the final benefits list and pricing bands. Please be ready to confirm by EOD tomorrow so we can move forward with the sales pitch and training work.
Confirmed. I'll have my review done by 2 PM tomorrow. Once D1 and D2 are locked, I can finalize the pitch framework and we can move to training planning in TH2.
I'll be ready with my input by 9 AM. Once the tier structure is approved, I can finalize the operations playbook in A3 and start on the data fields for A4.

Great. Let's reconvene tomorrow at 3 PM to formally approve D1 and D2. After that, we'll have a clear path to finalize A2, A3, and A4 in the next few days. This keeps us on track for the 21-day launch timeline.

threads.thread_goal: Lock sales pitch, objection handling, and training approach for launch.

messages.text: Now that we have D1 and D2 locked, I'm ready to share the draft sales pitch framework for A2. I've structured it around the three tiers and included the top 10 objections we're likely to hear based on my experience with membership programs. The pitch emphasizes the value prop for each tier and ties back to the benefits we finalized. I'd like feedback from 30302 and 285875 before we move to training planning in T5.

Thanks for getting this out quickly. I've reviewed the pitch framework and it's solid. The objection-handling guide is particularly strong—I especially like how you've addressed the 'why should I upgrade?' question. One thing I'd suggest: can we add a section on how to handle tier downgrades gracefully? We discussed that risk in TH1, and I want to make sure the sales team has clear language for that conversation.

Good catch. I'll add a section on downgrade conversations—framing it as 'adjusting to your current needs' rather than a penalty. I'll also tie it to the FAQ in T7 so customer service has consistent language. Should we also include a quick reference card that sales can use during calls? Something one-page that covers the tier benefits and key objection responses?

A quick reference card is a great idea. That will help with consistency across the team. I'm also thinking about how this ties into the operations playbook in A3. The pitch framework should align with the actual processes we've documented for onboarding and upgrades. Let me review A2 against A3 to make sure there are no gaps.

Perfect. That alignment is critical. Once you've reviewed A3, let me know if there are any process changes we need to reflect in the pitch. I want to make sure we're not promising something that operations can't deliver.

This is exactly the kind of cross-team alignment we need. 61232, can you finalize the pitch framework with the downgrade section and quick reference card by EOD tomorrow? And 285875, can you do the A2/A3 alignment check by tomorrow morning so we can incorporate any feedback?
I'll have the alignment check done by 9 AM tomorrow. I'm also going to flag any process gaps I find so we can address them before training.

I'll have the updated A2 with the downgrade section and quick reference card by EOD tomorrow. Once that's locked, we can move to training planning. I'm thinking we should do a joint session with sales and membership teams—maybe 2 hours covering the pitch, the operations playbook, and Q&A. What does everyone think?

Joint training makes sense. That way, sales understands the operational constraints and membership understands the pitch. We should also include customer service so they're aligned on the value prop. For T5, I'd suggest we plan for two sessions—one for sales/membership and one for customer service—so we can tailor the content. What's your timeline for getting the training materials ready?

I can have the training materials ready by end of next week. That gives us time to finalize A2 and A3, and then I'll create a slide deck and handouts. For T5, I'm thinking we schedule the first session for the following week—that gives everyone time to review the materials beforehand. Does that work with the 21-day timeline?

That timeline works. So we're looking at: finalize A2 by EOD tomorrow, finalize A3 by end of next week, training materials ready by end of next week, and first training session the week after. That puts us at day 10-12 of the 21-day timeline, which gives us buffer for the pilot and adjustments. Let me now propose D3 and D4 for approval. D3 is the approval of the standard sales pitch framework in A2. D4 is the agreement on mandatory vs optional training sessions in T5.

I'm ready to propose D3. The pitch framework is solid and addresses the key objections. For D4, I'd recommend that the joint sales/membership training is mandatory for all team members, and the customer service training is also mandatory since they'll be fielding questions. Does that align with what you're thinking?

I agree. Both trainings should be mandatory. We can't have inconsistent messaging in the field. I'm also thinking we should do a quick refresher session after the pilot in T10 to address any issues that come up. That could be optional for people who attended the first session.

Good idea on the refresher. So for D4, we're saying: mandatory joint training for sales and membership, mandatory training for customer service, and optional refresher after pilot. I'll formalize D3 and D4 for approval by EOD tomorrow once I have the updated A2 from 61232 and the A2/A3 alignment check from 285875.
Perfect. I'll have the updated A2 with the downgrade section and quick reference card by EOD tomorrow. Once D3 and D4 are approved, I can finalize the training materials and schedule the sessions.
I'll have the A2/A3 alignment check done by 9 AM tomorrow. Once that's done, we can move forward with confidence on the training approach.

Great. Let me summarize: we're finalizing A2 by EOD tomorrow, doing the A2/A3 alignment check by 9 AM tomorrow, and then formalizing D3 and D4 for approval by EOD tomorrow. Once those are locked, we move to training materials and scheduling. This keeps us on track for the 21-day timeline.

I've been following along. Once the pitch framework is locked in D3, I'll need to incorporate it into the launch communication plan. I want to make sure the external messaging aligns with what the sales team is saying internally.
Good point. Once D3 is locked, I'll share the final pitch framework with you so you can align the external messaging. We should make sure the value props are consistent across all channels.

Absolutely. 472865, once D3 is approved, 61232 will share the final pitch framework with you for the launch communication plan in A5. That's part of T6, so make sure you're coordinating with the marketing team on timing and channels.

Understood. I'll wait for the final pitch framework and then align with marketing on the launch communication plan. I'm also thinking about the timing—we should probably start the external campaign a few days before the full launch to build awareness.

Good thinking. We can discuss the campaign timing in TH5 when we finalize the cross-team launch timeline. For now, let's focus on locking D3 and D4. I'll send out the formal approval request by EOD tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on data fields, tagging rules, and pre-launch data clean-up scope.

messages.text: I've completed the initial data field matrix for A4 and the pre-launch data audit for T8. The audit shows some gaps in our current membership database—about 15% of records are missing key fields like tenure date and annual spend, which we need for tier eligibility. I've also identified some data quality issues in the segment tagging. I'm proposing we do a focused clean-up before launch to ensure accurate tier assignment. Can everyone review the audit findings and let me know what's feasible to address in the next week?

Thanks for getting the audit done. The 15% gap is concerning—we need accurate data for tier assignment. What's the root cause of the missing fields? Is it a data entry issue, a system limitation, or something else? And how much effort would it take to clean up the priority fields before launch?

The root cause is a mix of things. Some records were imported from legacy systems without full data mapping, and some fields weren't being captured consistently during onboarding. For the priority fields—tenure date and annual spend—I estimate we can clean up about 80% of the gaps in 3-4 days with a focused effort. The remaining 20% would require manual research or outreach to members, which is more time-consuming.

80% clean-up in 3-4 days is reasonable. For the remaining 20%, can we assign them to a default tier and then manually review them after launch? That way we don't hold up the launch, but we still have a plan to address the gaps.

That's a good approach. We can assign the 20% to the Basic tier as a default and then review them in the first week post-launch. I'll also need to define the tagging rules in A4 so that the data clean-up is consistent. For example, how do we define 'annual spend' for tier eligibility? Is it calendar year, rolling 12 months, or something else?

Good question. Let me check with finance on the definition of 'annual spend' for tier eligibility. I want to make sure it aligns with how they calculate customer value. In the meantime, can you draft the tagging rules in A4 based on what we've discussed so far? I'll review and finalize once I have the finance input.

I'll draft the tagging rules by tomorrow morning. I'm also thinking about the data fields we need to track post-launch—things like tier assignment date, upgrade/downgrade history, and benefit usage. Should we include those in A4 now, or add them after launch?

Let's include them in A4 now. We'll need those fields for reporting and for T12, which is the post-launch performance review cadence. If we define them upfront, we can make sure the system is configured correctly before launch.
Good thinking. Having those fields defined upfront will help with the sales pitch too. We can talk about how we track member engagement and tier progression, which is a value prop for the program.

Exactly. So for A4, I'll include: current data fields, new fields for tier assignment and tracking, tagging rules for tier eligibility, and the data clean-up plan. I'll have a draft by tomorrow morning for review.

Perfect. Once I have the finance input on 'annual spend' definition, I'll review your draft and we can finalize A4. I'm also going to propose D5 and D6 for approval. D5 is the confirmation of the final set of required membership data fields in A4. D6 is the decision on which data clean-up actions from T8 are in-scope before launch.

Understood. I'll have the draft A4 and the data clean-up plan by tomorrow morning. For D6, I'm proposing that we do the 80% clean-up of priority fields before launch, and defer the remaining 20% to post-launch with a default tier assignment.

That makes sense. The 80/20 approach balances launch readiness with data quality. I'm also thinking about how this impacts the sales targeting for the launch campaign. Once we have the clean data, we can segment more accurately for T6.

Good point. 472865, once we finalize the data clean-up in D6, we'll have accurate segment data for the launch campaign. Can you coordinate with 285875 on the segment definitions so the targeting is aligned with the tier structure?

Absolutely. Once the data is clean and the segments are defined, I can finalize the targeting for the launch campaign. I'll need the segment definitions from 285875 by end of next week so I can plan the campaign timing.
I'll have the segment definitions in A4 by end of next week. That should give you enough time to finalize the campaign plan.

Great. So here's the timeline: 285875 delivers draft A4 and data clean-up plan by tomorrow morning, I review with finance input by tomorrow afternoon, and we formalize D5 and D6 by EOD tomorrow. Once those are locked, we can start the data clean-up work and finalize the segment definitions for the launch campaign.
I'll have everything ready by 9 AM tomorrow. Once D5 and D6 are approved, I can start the data clean-up and finalize the segment definitions.
Perfect. Let me also flag that the data quality work ties into the pre-launch readiness checklist in A6. Once we finalize D5 and D6, I'll update A6 to reflect the data clean-up tasks and timeline.
Good idea. A6 should be a single source of truth for all pre-launch tasks. Once we have D1 through D6 locked, we can update A6 with all the dependencies and timelines.

Exactly. A6 will be our master checklist for launch readiness. Let me summarize where we are on TH3: 285875 is delivering draft A4 and data clean-up plan by tomorrow morning, I'm getting finance input on 'annual spend' definition, and we're formalizing D5 and D6 by EOD tomorrow. Once those are locked, we move to the pilot planning in TH4.

threads.thread_goal: Define pilot scope, success criteria, and adjustments before full rollout.

messages.text: Now that we have D1 through D6 locked, I want to move to pilot planning for T10. I'm proposing a pilot with 500 existing members from our top three segments, running for 2 weeks. This will give us time to test the tier assignment logic, validate the benefits delivery, and gather feedback before the full launch. I've drafted a pilot plan with success criteria and feedback collection methods. Can everyone review and share thoughts?

The pilot scope looks good. 500 members across three segments is a solid sample size. For the 2-week duration, I'm wondering if that's enough time to see meaningful engagement with the benefits. Some benefits might take longer to activate. What are the success criteria you're using?

Good question. The success criteria are: (1) 90% of pilot members are correctly assigned to their tier based on eligibility rules, (2) 80% of members report understanding their tier benefits, (3) zero critical issues with benefit delivery, and (4) positive feedback on the tier structure and value prop. The 2-week window is mainly to validate the mechanics, not necessarily to measure long-term engagement.

Those success criteria make sense. I'm also thinking about the operational side—how will we handle tier changes or issues during the pilot? Should we have a dedicated support person monitoring the pilot cohort?

Good thinking. Yes, I'm proposing we have a dedicated person monitoring the pilot cohort and handling any issues that come up. That person will also collect feedback from the pilot members and the internal teams. This will feed into A7, the pilot results and recommendations report.
Who's going to be the dedicated pilot monitor? And how will they collect feedback from the pilot members? Will it be surveys, interviews, or something else?

I'm thinking 285875 could lead the pilot monitoring since they've been managing the data and operations work. For feedback collection, I'm proposing a mix of surveys (sent to all 500 pilot members) and interviews (with a subset of 20-30 members from each segment). That should give us both quantitative and qualitative data.

I can lead the pilot monitoring. I'll set up the survey and coordinate the interviews. I'll also track the tier assignment accuracy and benefit delivery metrics. For the interviews, should we focus on specific questions about the tier structure, benefits, and pricing? Or should we keep it more open-ended?

I'd suggest a mix. Have some structured questions about the tier structure and benefits, but also leave room for open-ended feedback. That way we can validate our assumptions and also catch unexpected issues or opportunities.
Good approach. 285875, can you draft the survey and interview guide by end of next week? That will give us time to finalize the pilot plan and get it approved before we launch the pilot.
I'll have the survey and interview guide ready by end of next week. I'm also thinking about the timeline for the pilot. When do we want to start? And how will we select the 500 pilot members?

I'm thinking we start the pilot in about 10 days, which gives us time to finalize the tier structure, training, and data clean-up. For selecting the 500 members, I'm proposing we use a stratified random sample from each of the three key segments. That way we get representation across the segments and can validate the tier assignment logic for each.

That makes sense. A stratified sample will give us good coverage. I'm also thinking about how we communicate the pilot to the members. Should we tell them they're in a pilot, or just roll out the new tiers and see how they respond?

Good question. I think we should be transparent and tell them they're in a pilot. That way, if there are issues, they'll be more forgiving, and we can ask for their feedback more directly. We can frame it as 'we're testing a new membership program and would love your input.'

That's a good approach. I'll draft a pilot communication for the members that explains the new tiers and asks for their feedback. I'll also coordinate with the customer service team so they know to expect questions from the pilot members.

Perfect. So here's the pilot plan: 500 members from three segments, 2-week duration starting in about 10 days, stratified random sampling, transparent communication about the pilot, and feedback collection via surveys and interviews. I'm now proposing D7 and D8 for approval. D7 is the approval of the pilot cohort size, duration, and segments for T10. D8 is the agreement on which changes from A7 must be applied before full launch.

I'm ready to approve D7. The pilot scope is solid and the success criteria are clear. For D8, I think we should agree upfront that any critical issues found in the pilot must be fixed before full launch, but minor issues can be addressed post-launch. Does that align with your thinking?

I agree. Critical issues must be fixed before full launch. I'm thinking we define 'critical' as anything that impacts tier assignment accuracy, benefit delivery, or member experience. Minor issues like UI tweaks or messaging refinements can wait.

That's a good definition of critical. So for D8, we're saying: critical issues from the pilot must be fixed before full launch, and we'll document all findings in A7 with recommendations for adjustments. I'll formalize D7 and D8 for approval by EOD tomorrow.

Understood. I'll have the survey and interview guide ready by end of next week, and the pilot communication drafted by then as well. Once D7 and D8 are approved, I can finalize the pilot plan and start preparing for the launch.

Great. Let me summarize TH4: we've defined the pilot scope (500 members, 2 weeks, three segments), success criteria, and feedback collection methods. 285875 will draft the survey and interview guide by end of next week, and we'll formalize D7 and D8 by EOD tomorrow. Once those are locked, we move to the final cross-team timeline in TH5.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize cross-team launch timeline, KPIs, and review cadence.

messages.text: Now that we have D1 through D8 locked, I want to finalize the cross-team launch timeline and KPIs. I've drafted an integrated timeline in T11 that maps all the key milestones: tier design (done), training (next week), pilot (week 2-3), and full launch (week 3-4). I've also drafted the KPI list for T12 covering tier adoption, member satisfaction, and sales performance. Can everyone review and confirm the timeline and KPIs?

I've reviewed the timeline and it looks solid. The training is scheduled for next week, which gives us time to finalize the materials. The pilot in week 2-3 is good, and the full launch in week 3-4 is aggressive but doable. For the KPIs, I'm looking at tier adoption rate, average order value by tier, and sales team conversion rate. Are those the right metrics?

Those are good metrics. I'm also thinking about member satisfaction and retention. We should track NPS (Net Promoter Score) for each tier and churn rate. That will help us understand if the tiers are delivering value. For the sales metrics, we should also track the incentive payout to make sure we're not overspending.

I agree on the member satisfaction and retention metrics. I'm also thinking about operational metrics—things like tier assignment accuracy, benefit delivery success rate, and customer service ticket volume. Those will help us understand if the operations are running smoothly.

Excellent. So the KPI list includes: tier adoption rate, average order value by tier, sales conversion rate, NPS by tier, churn rate, tier assignment accuracy, benefit delivery success rate, and customer service ticket volume. That's a comprehensive set. For T12, I'm proposing we do weekly reviews for the first 8 weeks post-launch, then move to monthly reviews. Does that work?

Weekly reviews for the first 8 weeks makes sense. That gives us time to catch issues early and make adjustments. After 8 weeks, we should have enough data to understand the trends and move to monthly reviews. I'm also thinking about the review format—should we have a dedicated meeting or just share a report?

I'm thinking a dedicated 30-minute meeting each week where we review the KPIs, discuss any issues, and agree on next steps. That way we can have a real-time discussion and make decisions quickly. The meeting should include the core team: you, me, 285875, and 472865 for the marketing/campaign perspective.

A dedicated meeting makes sense. I'll prepare the KPI report each week with the data and any operational issues. I'm also thinking about the escalation path—if we see a critical issue, who do we escalate to?

Good question. For critical issues, we escalate to the leadership team immediately—don't wait for the weekly review. For the weekly review, we focus on trends and adjustments. I'll document the escalation path in A6 so everyone knows the process.

That makes sense. So the weekly review is for monitoring and optimization, and critical issues go up immediately. I'm also thinking about the first review meeting—should we schedule it for the day after launch, or wait a few days to let things settle?

I'm thinking we do the first review 3 days after launch. That gives us time to see initial adoption and any issues, but we're still close enough to the launch to make quick adjustments if needed. I'll schedule the first two review meetings in T12 and we can confirm the rest once we see how things are going.
That works. I'll have the KPI report ready for the first review meeting. I'm also going to set up a dashboard so we can track the metrics in real-time during the first few weeks.

Great idea on the dashboard. That will help us spot issues quickly. Now let me finalize the timeline. Here's the summary: week 1 (today) - finalize tier design and training materials, week 2 - conduct training and start pilot, week 3 - pilot runs and we gather feedback, week 4 - full launch. Does everyone agree with this timeline?

The timeline is aggressive but achievable. The key dependencies are: tier design (done), training materials (end of week 1), pilot launch (start of week 2), and full launch (start of week 4). I'm confident we can hit these milestones.
I agree. The timeline is tight but doable. The main risk is if we find critical issues in the pilot that require significant rework. But we've built in some buffer with the 2-week pilot window.

Good point. The pilot is our safety valve. If we find critical issues, we have time to fix them before the full launch. Now let me update A6 with the final timeline and KPI list, and we'll have a complete picture of the launch readiness.

I've been following along. Once the timeline is finalized, I'll coordinate the external launch campaign with the internal timeline. I want to make sure the external messaging goes out a few days before the full launch to build awareness.

Good thinking. So the external campaign should start about 3-4 days before the full launch. That gives members time to see the messaging and prepare for the new tiers. 472865, can you finalize the campaign timing in T6 based on the launch date?

Absolutely. Once the full launch date is confirmed, I'll finalize the campaign timing. I'm thinking we do a teaser campaign 5 days before launch, then the main campaign 3 days before, and then the launch announcement on day 1.

That's a good cadence. Teaser, main campaign, then launch announcement. That should build momentum and awareness. Let me finalize the cross-team timeline and KPI list by EOD today, and I'll send out the updated A6 with all the milestones and dependencies. Everyone, please confirm the timeline and KPIs by tomorrow morning so we can move forward with confidence.
Confirmed. I'll review the updated A6 by tomorrow morning and confirm the timeline. Once that's locked, we're ready to execute.
I'll review the timeline and KPIs by tomorrow morning as well. Once everything is confirmed, I'll start preparing for the pilot launch.

Perfect. So here's the final summary: we have D1 through D8 locked, the cross-team timeline is finalized, the KPI list is confirmed, and the review cadence is set. A6 is our master checklist for launch readiness. We're on track for the 21-day launch timeline. Let's execute.
